goal: Evaluate whether the support automation pilot justifies production rollout: compare resolution quality, escalation burden, complete costs, security and independent replication evidence.

sources.title: Constructed support pilot — outcome register
sources.text: The pilot processed 1200 customer requests across 20 business days. Reviewers accepted 1116 resolutions. Eighteen critical requests were incorrectly resolved without escalation. Sixty-six additional requests required correction. Median response time was 240 milliseconds. The pilot used a curated request set and did not establish production reliability.

sources.title: Constructed cost and review ledger
sources.text: Compute cost for the pilot was 96 USD. Fourteen hours of human review at 75 USD per hour cost 1050 USD. Integration work required 80 hours at 100 USD per hour. The prior manual process averaged six minutes per request. Ongoing monitoring and incident costs have not been measured. No realized revenue or net cost saving was observed.

sources.title: Constructed security assessment
sources.text: Security review found three unresolved issues: document permissions were not propagated, exported traces included personal data, and retrieval accepted unsigned sources. Production rollout remains blocked pending remediation and re-test. No independent penetration test has been completed.

sources.title: Constructed replication and deployment register
sources.text: Independent replications completed: zero. A future trial must freeze the pipeline before collecting a separate test set. Production acceptance requires audited critical-error rates, full operating costs and a rollback drill. The current evidence supports a bounded pilot only.
